Andrea Kimi Antonelli won from pole for Mercedes, joined on the podium by Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) second and Max Verstappen (Red Bull) third. The classification shows a clean conversion of Mercedes' front-row start into a win: Leclerc climbed three places from fourth to take second and the fastest lap, while Lando Norris also gained three spots, moving from eighth to fifth.
highlights: The biggest gain came from Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris, both climbing three places — Leclerc from fourth to second, Norris from eighth to fifth.
Charles Leclerc took the fastest lap of the race on his way to second place for Ferrari.
Three cars retired without a classified time: Valtteri Bottas, Franco Colapinto and Oliver Bearman all dropped out.

review.summary: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing, joined on the podium by Jorge Martin third for Aprilia Racing and Raul Fernandez second for SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team. Ai Ogura completed the top four for SuperFile Trackhouse. Yamaha's Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller both did not finish, as did Ducati's Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer.
highlights: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing.
Raul Fernandez finished second for SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team, with Ai Ogura fourth.
Yamaha's Jack Miller and Toprak Razgatlioglu did not finish, as did Ducati's Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer.

review.summary: Winner Taylor Barnard of DS Penske took a surprise victory, climbing from sixth on the grid for the full 25 points. Nyck De Vries led Mahindra's one-two, winning from pole to finish second ahead of team-mate Edoardo Mortara. The classification shows strong starters falling away: Pascal Wehrlein dropped from third to fourteenth and Nico Müller from fourth to twelfth.
highlights: Norman Nato made the biggest climb of the day, rising from nineteenth to tenth.
Taylor Barnard won for DS Penske, climbing from sixth on the grid to take the full 25 points.
De Vries won from pole to complete Mahindra's one-two ahead of team-mate Edoardo Mortara.
Joel Eriksson and Lucas Di Grassi both failed to finish, neither able to score.
